one_liner: Hand-written NEON inference for one tiny Fashion-MNIST CNN on a Raspberry Pi 4B; 2.1-3.1x faster than tuned TFLite, ncnn and ONNX Runtime.
what_it_does: A worked example, not a library: one fixed CNN (3x3 conv to 8 channels, leaky ReLU, 2x2 max pool, 3x3 conv to 16 channels, leaky ReLU, pool, 576x10 FC) implemented four ways (cnn_struct, cnn_const, cnn_neon, cnn_fuse), each a standalone main program of about 200 lines that loads exported weights (model.bin) and 70,000 images and writes logits. Three more programs run the same exported model through ONNX Runtime, ncnn and TFLite for comparison. There is no reusable API; you copy the kernel functions and rewrite them for your own layer shapes.
how_it_is_fast: cnn_neon replaces im2col + OpenBLAS sgemm with a direct convolution: weights are repacked so four output channels sit in one NEON register, and each 3x3 tap does vfmaq_laneq_f32 on four output pixels for four channels at once (4x4 register blocking), with a zero-bordered input copy to drop boundary checks; the FC layer uses pre-interleaved weights and ten NEON accumulators. cnn_fuse then fuses conv, 2x2 max pool and leaky ReLU into one kernel: it computes two conv rows in registers, pools them with vpmaxq_f32/vmax_f32, applies the activation after pooling (valid because leaky ReLU is monotonic, so it runs on 4x fewer values) and never writes the conv output to memory. Shapes are compile-time constants, and parallelism is one image per OpenMP thread.
when_to_use: You ship a fixed, tiny CNN (a few thousand parameters, few channels) to a known ARMv8 board and per-image latency or throughput matters more than flexibility.
You want a short, readable template for a fused conv + pool + activation NEON kernel to adapt to your own small model.

You profile a small model under ONNX Runtime, ncnn or TFLite and find im2col and framework overhead dominate; this repo shows the per-layer measurement-versus-MAC-ceiling method for deciding what to hand-write.
Teaching or self-study of step-by-step inference optimization (struct, then constants, then NEON, then fusion), each step with a measured time.
when_not_to_use: Any model other than this exact architecture: kernel shapes, offsets into model.bin and buffer sizes are hard-coded, so a new model means rewriting the kernels.
x86 or 32-bit ARM targets: the kernels use AArch64-only NEON intrinsics (vfmaq_laneq_f32, vaddvq_f32, vpmaxq_f32) and there is no scalar fallback.
Medium or large models where im2col cost is small next to GEMM; the README itself says frameworks do well there.
When you need quantized (int8) or fp16 inference, dynamic shapes, batching APIs or model-format import; none exist here.
Production use that needs tests beyond the one logit-tolerance check, versioned releases or support: 10 stars, 18 commits written in one week of August 2026.

integration.dependencies: OpenMP and fmt (vendored header-only in src/3rdparty) for cnn_neon and cnn_fuse; OpenBLAS for cnn_struct and cnn_const; ONNX Runtime 1.27.1, ncnn 20260526 and TFLite 2.20.0 for the comparison programs; Python 3.11 with torch 2.13.0 to train and export the model
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, CMake 3.20, a GCC or Clang with AArch64 arm_neon.h and OpenMP (compiler version not documented)
integration.platforms: AArch64 with NEON only (tested on Raspberry Pi 4B, Cortex-A72, 64-bit OS implied by the A64 intrinsics)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each program uses file-scope static buffers with per-OpenMP-thread scratch slots indexed by omp_get_thread_num() and capped at 8 threads, so run() is safe only inside its own OpenMP loop

gotchas: Harness asymmetry: the ONNX Runtime row runs Session::Run sequentially on sub-batches of 8 images with intra-op threads, while every other row runs one image per OpenMP thread (ncnn with a single-threaded net, TFLite with one interpreter per thread); an image-per-thread ORT configuration (concurrent Run calls, one intra-op thread each) was not measured, so part of the 3.1x versus ORT may reflect threading strategy rather than kernels.

The hand-written builds get -mcpu=native and -funsafe-math-optimizations while ORT, ncnn, TFLite and OpenBLAS are prebuilt libraries from ~/Documents/libs with unstated build options; the compiler and version, and the --threads and --runs values used for the README table, are not stated (the program default is 1 thread; the README text mentions 4 threads for the frameworks).

The README says cnn_neon uses a hand-written GEMM from optimize-gemm; the code is a self-contained direct convolution (4x4 register-blocked lane FMAs), and no optimize-gemm code is included. Correctness is checked: the hand-written programs compare all 70,000 x 10 logits against PyTorch reference logits with a 1e-4 max-abs tolerance, while the framework programs only report argmax agreement (tolerance disabled).

CMakeLists.txt makes ncnn, ONNX Runtime and OpenBLAS REQUIRED for the whole project, so building only cnn_fuse needs an edited CMakeLists or a manual compile; the images, reference logits and model files come from the 'data' release (data_20260829.tar.gz, 46 MB) or from rerunning python/train.py.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: None of the siblings is an inference engine; pick this over IntrinsicML (generic SIMD ML microkernels, mostly x86) when you need a complete fused NEON forward pass for a tiny CNN on Cortex-A72, and over ARM NEON Compositor when your NEON workload is convolution rather than image blending.
verified_claims_summary: On a Raspberry Pi 4B (4x Cortex-A72 at 1.8 GHz), classifying 70,000 Fashion-MNIST images in blocks of 32 with best-of-N wall time, cnn_fuse took 783 ms and cnn_neon 1045 ms against TFLite 2.20.0 at 1621 ms, ncnn 20260526 at 2302 ms and ONNX Runtime 1.27.1 at 2440 ms (about 2.1x, 2.9x and 3.1x for cnn_fuse, derived from page data), with each framework tuned by the author; compiler unstated. By the README's own one-FMLA-per-cycle ceiling (137 + 403 + 14 ms for conv1, conv2 and FC at 4 threads), cnn_fuse runs at roughly 70% of peak (derived from page data).
status_note: Active only in a burst (18 commits, 22-29 August 2026, none since) and MIT-licensed; useful as a copyable template for small fixed models on AArch64, not as a maintained dependency.
